evidence.workload: Short document field extraction into constrained JSON, one request at a time, 32-token output limit, greedy decoding. Minimize memory while retaining 95% of BF16 extraction accuracy and throughput. User wants to fit AI on current hardware. Mixed recipes protect token embeddings, output head, and value/down projections in the first/last eighth of layers and every third middle layer. Other layers use base bits.

prior.source: Completed first search block; no heldout tasks measured in this batch.

pattern_definitions.all-v-down: All value and down projections plus embedding/head use protected bits; other modules use base bits.
pattern_definitions.all-except-mlp-expansion: Only MLP gate_proj and up_proj use base bits; all other quantizable modules use protected bits.
pattern_definitions.default: Sparse boundary/every-third v/down plus embedding/head protection.

evidence.selection: Jointly rank all recipes, top two will be measured with identical software gates.

role_plan.reason:
These are 15 assigned specialist perspectives. Their proposals and shared ranking are a synthesis, not independent agent votes. All recommendations are hypotheses.

Specialist proposals:
1. Weight memory: propose mixed3-4-g64; test whether a mostly 3-bit recipe reduces peak memory while passing both gates.
2. Embedding precision: propose mlp3-rest4-g128, which retains 4-bit embedding/head protection.
3. Attention precision: propose vdown4-rest3-g128 to test protection of every value projection.
4. MLP precision: propose mlp3-rest4-g128, limiting 3-bit weights to gate/up projections.
5. Quantization error: propose int3-g32 to test whether smaller groups recover accuracy.
6. Group size: propose mixed3-4-g64 to compare with the measured g128 recipe.
7. Decode latency: propose mlp3-rest4-g128; assess throughput under the unchanged greedy, 32-token workload.
8. Prefill latency: propose mixed3-4-g64; assess it with the existing short-document timing procedure.
9. Structured extraction: propose mlp3-rest4-g128; broader protection may preserve field values and constrained JSON output.
10. Quality gates: support mlp3-rest4-g128 for measurement; require the unchanged 0.95 quality and BF16 throughput-retention gates.
11. Measurement noise: support mixed3-4-g64 provisionally; the two identical int4 recipes produced different throughput, so small differences do not establish gains.
12. Search efficiency: propose the pair mlp3-rest4-g128 and mixed3-4-g64 to test two distinct recovery mechanisms within two candidates.
13. Hardware fit: propose mixed3-4-g64; use measured peak MLX memory, not nominal bit width, to assess fit.
14. Artifact integrity: support mlp3-rest4-g128 only with its exact supplied protection pattern and unchanged model/runtime.
15. Failure analysis: propose vdown4-rest3-g128 as a protection-coverage hypothesis; deprioritize 2-bit recipes after mixed2-4-g128 scored zero quality.

Shared ranking of all recipes for this next batch:
1. mlp3-rest4-g128
2. mixed3-4-g64
3. vdown4-rest3-g128
4. int3-g32

8. int3-g128

Measure ranks 1 and 2 only. Rank 1 tests broader 4-bit protection; rank 2 tests smaller groups with the existing sparse protection. Neither has measured results. This is an experiment-priority ranking, not a demonstrated performance ranking.

Int4-g128 is the only observed quality-passing recipe, at 2299.484 MiB peak. Int3-g128 and mixed3-4-g128 fall below the 0.95 quality gate. BF16 throughput is absent, so throughput eligibility cannot be established for any recipe. No heldout tasks were measured, and hardware capacity is unspecified. Keep tasks, gates, budget, model, and runtime unchanged; select lower measured peak memory only among candidates that pass both existing gates.
